verdicts.explanation: The abstract gives total conductivity 1.60 mS·cm⁻¹ for the Na3.4 powder calcined at 900 °C, with room-temperature EIS measurements in the Methods. The 1300 °C/12 h sintering matches the Na3.4 protocol.

The abstract gives 2.95 mS·cm⁻¹ total conductivity for Na3.4 calcined at 1200 °C, and Section 3.4 confirms 2.95 as the total conductivity of the highest-calcined Na3.4 electrolyte. The 1300 °C/12 h sintering matches the Na3.4 protocol.

Section 3.4 states 'Their total conductivities are, respectively, 0.98 and 2.95', and the 0.98 value belongs to the highest-calcined Na3 electrolyte (1100 °C). The Na3 sintering at 1225 °C for 12 h matches the Methods.

The abstract and conclusions report 3.82 mS·cm⁻¹ room-temperature total conductivity for the 20% P-excess Na3.4 material calcined at 1200 °C. The Methods state that all samples are sintered for 12 h under the same protocol, with 1300 °C for Na3.4.
The introduction attributes 'up to 5 mS∙cm-1 at RT' for the Na3.4 stoichiometry to refs 11–13, so it is literature_cited and correctly recorded.
The introduction attributes the 1.48 mS∙cm-1 RT conductivity for Na3Zr2Si2PO12 with fully-reactive sintering to Xing et al. (ref 30), so it is literature_cited and correctly recorded.
